segments.headline: The day's news from the watch desk

graphic.title: Iran's rejected offer · Two storms · A busy data week
bullets: Iran says it won't soften Hormuz demands after Trump's rejection
Russian strikes hit Ukraine hard again, Kyiv's third night running
Hurricane Nolo nears Category five as the nor'easter lingers
Colts snap their losing streak, Astros win the AL West on the last day

lines.text: Welcome to Heartbeat News. I'm AI Robot Vex.
And I'm Alien Joe. It's Monday, September twenty-eighth.

Today: Iran digs in after President Trump rejects its plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, Russian strikes kill eight in Ukraine, and Hurricane Nolo closes in on Category five strength south of Hawaii.
Plus oil jumps, the Fed proposes stablecoin rules, a new drug for a rare bone disease, and a very good day for two football and baseball teams. Let's get to it.

segments.strap: HURRICANE NOLO NEARS CATEGORY FIVE AS NOR'EASTER LINGERS
segments.headline: Two storms, still going

graphic.title: One storm peaking, one storm staying
bullets: Nolo near Category five early Monday, well south of Hawaii and moving away
Wind alerts remain for the Big Island and Maui County, high surf on south shores
Nor'easter day three: one confirmed death, tidal flooding in New Jersey
Logan Airport logged hundreds of delays and cancellations Sunday

lines.text: We start with the weather. Two storms are still making headlines this morning.

Hurricane Nolo has strengthened to Category four, sustained winds near one hundred fifty miles an hour, just shy of Category five. It's well south of Hawaii now and moving away, but wind alerts remain for parts of the Big Island and Maui County, with high surf along south-facing shores.

Back on the mainland, that nor'easter is on its third day. New York City's Housing Authority confirmed one death, a worker killed by a falling tree Saturday. More than a hundred ten thousand households, from North Carolina to New England, were still without power Sunday, and Boston's Logan Airport logged hundreds of delays and cancellations.
Tidal flooding was reported in New Jersey, and a coastal flood advisory for Long Island runs into this afternoon.

segments.strap: IRAN WON'T SOFTEN HORMUZ DEMANDS AFTER TRUMP'S REJECTION
segments.headline: A standoff restarts

graphic.title: Rejected offer, restated terms
bullets: Iran: still wants blockade lifted, frozen funds released, attacks on all fronts ended
Foreign Minister Araghchi: "fully prepared" for war, also "ready for diplomacy"
Claims of missiles and drones fired at ships near Qeshm Island, not independently confirmed
Iran says it captured a second U.S. underwater drone; the U.S. disputes that

lines.text: Iran says it will not soften its terms for reopening the Strait of Hormuz, a day after President Trump rejected Tehran's seven-point proposal.

Iran's foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, put it this way: Tehran is fully prepared for the war to resume, but also, in his words, ready for diplomacy. The conditions haven't changed — lift the blockade, release frozen funds, end attacks on every front, including in Lebanon.

Reports out of the region describe anti-ship missiles and drones fired at vessels near Qeshm Island, and Iran says it captured a second American underwater drone. The U.S. disputes that an advanced drone was taken. None of that is independently confirmed yet, so treat both sides' claims as claims.
Bottom line: yesterday's rejection didn't end the standoff. It restarted it.

segments.strap: RUSSIAN STRIKES KILL EIGHT IN UKRAINE, KYIV HIT A THIRD NIGHT
segments.headline: Another heavy night of strikes

graphic.title: A third straight night on Kyiv
bullets: Kyivstar headquarters struck; a Vodafone data center hit the night before
Zelenskyy: nearly 3,900 drones, bombs and missiles fired at Ukraine this past week
Ukraine says it hit an oil depot and a missile-component plant inside Russia

lines.text: Russia hit Ukraine hard again. Ukrainian officials say strikes killed eight people Sunday, including two at a market near Kyiv, with nine more hurt in the capital.

It was the third straight night of strikes on Kyiv. Roughly a hundred seventy Shahed drones flew overnight, and a Russian strike hit the headquarters of the telecom company Kyivstar. That follows a strike on a Vodafone data center the night before — the second such facility hit in two nights.

President Zelenskyy says Russia has fired nearly thirty-nine hundred drones, bombs and missiles at Ukraine in the past week alone, and that Moscow isn't ready to end the war. Ukraine, for its part, says it hit an oil depot and a missile-component plant inside Russia.

segments.strap: OIL JUMPS PAST $94 A BARREL AS A BUSY DATA WEEK BEGINS
segments.headline: A jumpy Monday for oil, a calm one for stocks

graphic.title: This week's numbers
bullets: S&P 500 futures +0.5%, Nasdaq futures +0.4% in Monday premarket
Dallas Fed today, JOLTS Tuesday, GDP and inflation data Wednesday
September jobs report Friday, unemployment expected near 4.1%

lines.text: On Wall Street, futures point modestly higher to start the week: S and P five hundred futures up about half a percent, Nasdaq futures up about four tenths of a percent.

Oil is making the bigger move. U.S. crude jumped past ninety-four dollars a barrel, up almost two percent, and Brent crude near one hundred seven dollars, up two and a half percent — both rising on Iran's rejected Hormuz offer. Gasoline futures followed, near three dollars and forty-one cents a gallon.

It's a heavy week for economic data. The Dallas Fed reports today, job openings come Tuesday, growth and inflation data Wednesday, and the September jobs report Friday, with unemployment expected around four point one percent.

segments.strap: FED PROPOSES STABLECOIN RULES; BINANCE BACKS CIRCLE
segments.headline: Moves in the stablecoin race

graphic.title: Stablecoins in the news
bullets: Fed framework lets bank subsidiaries apply to issue stablecoins under the GENIUS Act
Ethereum stablecoin supply near $146.5 billion even as trading volume falls

lines.text: The Federal Reserve proposed a framework letting bank subsidiaries apply to issue stablecoins under the GENIUS Act, with supervisory standards attached. There's a sixty-day public comment period.

And in the stablecoin race itself, Binance took a hundred-million-dollar stake in Circle, the company behind U.S.D.C. Analysts read it as Circle picking up a major distribution partner, at Tether's expense.

One more data point: stablecoin supply on Ethereum is near a hundred forty-six and a half billion dollars, even as trading volume on Ethereum's exchanges has fallen by about half over the past month. Money parked, not moving.

segments.strap: F.D.A. APPROVES NEW DRUG FOR A RARE BONE DISEASE
segments.headline: A new option for a rare condition

graphic.title: Two new approvals
bullets: Zilurgisertib (Atebrioz) approved for fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva, ages 12+
Third therapy for the condition; available starting in October
Trial showed bone volume dropped on the drug, rose sharply on placebo
A new messenger-RNA flu vaccine, M-FLUSIVA, approved for adults 50 and up

lines.text: Health news: the F.D.A. approved zilurgisertib, brand name Atebrioz, for fibrodysplasia ossificans progressiva — a rare disease where soft tissue turns to bone. It's approved for patients twelve and older, the third therapy for the condition, and it becomes available in October.
In its trial, patients on the drug lost bone volume where placebo patients gained a significant amount — a reversal, not just a slowdown.
Separately, a new messenger-RNA flu vaccine, M-FLUSIVA, was approved for adults fifty and older.

segments.strap: COLTS SNAP LOSING STREAK; ASTROS CLINCH AL WEST ON FINAL DAY
segments.headline: A very good Sunday, twice over

graphic.title: Down to the wire
bullets: Colts beat Texans 19-17 on a last-second field goal, snapping the NFL's longest losing streak
Astros win the AL West on the season's final day, finishing 81-81
MLB Wild Card games start Tuesday: Phillies-Braves, White Sox-Astros, Red Sox-Yankees, Cubs-Padres
Tonight: Monday Night Football, Eagles at Bears

lines.text: In the N.F.L., the Colts beat the Texans nineteen to seventeen Sunday. Kicker Spencer Shrader, playing through a groin injury, hit four field goals, including the game winner from forty-three yards with sixteen seconds left. It's Indianapolis's first win since last November, snapping the league's longest active losing streak.

In baseball, the Astros won the American League West on the very last day, beating the Athletics nine to nothing while the Twins beat the Rangers. Houston finishes eighty-one and eighty-one — the first division winner at exactly five hundred in a hundred sixty-two game season.
Wild Card games start tomorrow: Phillies at Braves, White Sox at Astros, Red Sox at Yankees, and Cubs at Padres, all best of three.
And tonight, Monday Night Football: the Eagles at the Bears.

segments.strap: AVENGERS: ENDGAME ENCORE TOPS THE BOX OFFICE
segments.headline: A superhero rerun wins the weekend

graphic.title: Weekend box office
bullets: Heart of the Beast opened third, $20 million
Endgame Encore adds four scenes teasing Avengers: Doomsday, out in December

lines.text: At the box office, that 'Avengers: Endgame' encore led the weekend with about twenty-six million dollars domestic, eighty-six million worldwide.

'Resident Evil' held second place in its second weekend, at twenty-three million, three hundred thousand dollars, pushing its domestic total past one hundred three million. Paramount's 'Heart of the Beast' opened third, at twenty million.
And that Endgame re-release tacked on four new scenes teasing 'Avengers: Doomsday,' out in December.

segments.strap: SPACEX TARGETS FIRST STARSHIP ORBITAL ATTEMPT TODAY
segments.headline: Starship's biggest test yet

graphic.title: Flight 14, by the numbers
bullets: F.A.A.-cleared for a first full orbital attempt from Starbase, Texas
About six orbits over ten hours, then an in-space burn and splashdown off Chile
Outcome not known as of this taping

lines.text: SpaceX is set for its most ambitious Starship flight yet. Flight fourteen is F.A.A.-cleared for a first full orbital attempt, targeting seven forty-six this morning, Central time, from Starbase, Texas.

The plan: about six orbits over ten hours, the rocket's first payload deployment, twenty-six Starlink satellites, an in-space engine burn, and a splashdown off the coast of Chile. We didn't have the outcome as of this taping.
Separately, NASA's Crew Thirteen astronauts have arrived in Florida ahead of a launch no earlier than October first.

segments.strap: WHITE HOUSE FACES QUESTIONS OVER TAXPAYER-FUNDED ADS
segments.headline: A dispute over paid messaging

graphic.title: A third taxpayer-funded spot
bullets: "Final Battle" ad uses Trump campaign imagery and language, Washington Post reports
More than $300,000 spent, per that report
Ethics officials and Democratic lawmakers question its legality
White House calls the spots public-service announcements

lines.text: The Washington Post reports the White House has now run a third taxpayer-funded ad, called 'Final Battle,' using President Trump's campaign imagery and language. The paper says more than three hundred thousand dollars was spent.

Former ethics officials and Democratic lawmakers are questioning whether that crosses a federal line against unauthorized political publicity. The White House calls the spots public-service announcements, not campaign ads.
That's a dispute, not a ruling. Nobody's decided it in court yet.
